concept_html:
Polars is a DataFrame library written in Rust. It runs on all your cores and has no row index. You describe work with expressions: pl.col("weight").sum() is a recipe, not a result. Polars runs it inside a context.

import polars as pl

shares = (
    df.group_by("wave", "brand")
    .agg(pl.col("weight").sum().alias("brand_weight"))
    .with_columns(total=pl.col("brand_weight").sum().over("wave"))
)
  • select returns only the expressions you list. with_columns adds or replaces columns. filter keeps rows. group_by(...).agg(...) aggregates.
  • .over("wave") computes a group total and broadcasts it back to each row, like a window function in SQL.
  • pl.when(...).then(...).otherwise(...) replaces np.where.

Polars has two modes. A DataFrame runs each step at once. A LazyFrame, from df.lazy() or pl.scan_parquet(path), records the steps and runs nothing until .collect(). Before running, the optimiser rewrites the plan. It pushes filters down to the scan, so rows you drop are never read, and reads only the columns you use. lf.explain() prints the plan.

Two behaviours to know (Polars 1.33):

  • sum() of a group with only nulls returns 0, not null. Check null_count() before you trust a total.
  • mean() skips nulls. sum() / pl.len() counts null rows in the denominator and gives a different answer.

Use lazy mode for files. Scan, filter, select, aggregate, then collect once at the end.

lines: import polars as pl
def brand_weights(path: str, wave: str) -> pl.DataFrame:
"""Weighted totals and means per brand for one wave. Grain: one row per brand."""
return (
pl.scan_parquet(path)
.filter(pl.col("wave") == wave)
.group_by("brand")
.agg(
total=pl.col("weight").sum(),
mean_w=pl.col("weight").mean(),
missing=pl.col("weight").null_count(),
)
.sort("brand")
.collect()
)

exercises.solution:
import polars as pl


def brand_share(df: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Weighted share of each brand within its wave. Grain: one row per wave and brand.

    Args:
        df: Columns wave, brand, weight.

    Returns:
        Columns wave, brand, share. share is null when the wave total is 0.
    """
    return (
        df.group_by("wave", "brand")
        .agg(brand_weight=pl.col("weight").sum())
        .with_columns(total=pl.col("brand_weight").sum().over("wave"))
        .with_columns(
            share=pl.when(pl.col("total") > 0)
            .then(pl.col("brand_weight") / pl.col("total"))
            .otherwise(None)
        )
        .select("wave", "brand", "share")
        .sort("wave", "brand")
    )
solution_lines: import polars as pl
def brand_share(df: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
"""Weighted share of each brand within its wave. Grain: one row per wave and brand.
Args:
df: Columns wave, brand, weight.
Returns:
Columns wave, brand, share. share is null when the wave total is 0.
"""
return (
df.group_by("wave", "brand")
.agg(brand_weight=pl.col("weight").sum())
.with_columns(total=pl.col("brand_weight").sum().over("wave"))
.with_columns(
share=pl.when(pl.col("total") > 0)
.then(pl.col("brand_weight") / pl.col("total"))
.otherwise(None)
)
.select("wave", "brand", "share")
.sort("wave", "brand")
)

title: Polars expressions and lazy frames
why_html:
A weekly job reads a 9 GB Parquet extract with pl.read_parquet, then filters to the current wave. Memory peaks at 14 GB and the job fails on a 16 GB runner on the week the extract grows.

pl.scan_parquet(path).filter(pl.col("wave") == wave).select(cols).collect() lets Polars skip other waves' row groups and unused columns at read time, so memory scales with one wave, not the whole file.
